s1.syndrome_frame: Acute painful vision loss with floaters and retinal detachment
salient_findings: Painful vision loss in one eye
Retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid
Choroidal detachments in the nasal and temporal periphery
key_facts: 71-year-old woman
1-week history of symptoms
No history of myopia, ocular trauma, or surgery
Visual acuity 20/30–2 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye
Intraocular pressure 21 mm Hg OD and 17 mm Hg OS
Mild nuclear sclerotic cataract in the right eye
Rare anterior chamber cells and 1+ vitreous cells in the left eye
No retinal breaks identified
Normal laboratory studies
Mild posterior scleral enhancement on MRI
Late leakage in the temporal periphery on fluorescein angiography
Shallow subretinal fluid and posterior vitreous detachment on optical coherence tomography

differentials: Acute Posterior Multifocal Placoid Pigment Epitheliopathy
per_call: Acute Posterior Multifocal Placoid Pigment Epitheliopathy

shortlist.label: Posterior Scleritis
shortlist.why_kept: Mild posterior scleral enhancement on MRI and clinical presentation of painful vision loss with choroidal detachments

shortlist.label: Serous Retinal Detachment
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid and no retinal breaks identified

shortlist.label: Uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of rare anterior chamber cells and 1+ vitreous cells in the left eye

shortlist.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of painful vision loss with choroidal detachments and retinal detachment

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Normal laboratory studies and presence of rare anterior chamber cells and 1+ vitreous cells in the left eye, which could be indicative of granulomatous uveitis

raw.rationale: The presence of mild posterior scleral enhancement on MRI, late leakage in the temporal periphery on fluorescein angiography, and the resolution of choroidal detachments with prednisone treatment support the diagnosis of posterior scleritis.

rejected.label: Serous Retinal Detachment
rejected.why: While the patient has a serous retinal detachment, it is likely secondary to the posterior scleritis.

rejected.label: Uveitis
rejected.why: The rare anterior chamber cells and 1+ vitreous cells could suggest uveitis, but the overall clinical picture and imaging findings are more consistent with posterior scleritis.

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada Disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with bilateral involvement, granulomatous uveitis, and often skin, hair, and auditory findings, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of granulomatous uveitis or other systemic findings suggestive of sarcoidosis in this patient.

gold: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment with choroidal detachment
